answer: The velvet test I would run is Signed church warden service with diocese attestation: service the diocese recorded across years of parishes, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so service the diocese recorded across years of parishes stays private; the orchard is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the ripple of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
